availability.comment: Stroud completed 20 of 38 passes for 211 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding three rushes for 20 yards in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. Stroud looked like he was on his way to another highly productive day early while helping stake the Texans to a 17-0 lead in the first half, but the fourth-year signal-caller and his offense largely stagnated in the second half. Stroud spread the ball around while connecting with eight different targets overall, and his trio of scoring strikes went to Nico Collins (12 yards), Xavier Hutchinson (11 yards) and Dalton Schultz (11 yards), the latter accounting for Houston's only second-half points. Despite the Texans' monumental collapse, Stroud's highly impressive season continues, as he's up to 2,462 passing yards, a 19:3 TD:INT and 120 rushing yards and another score heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

Montgomery (groin) was a full participant at Monday's walkthrough. Montgomery was held out of Sunday's loss at Cleveland, which marked his fourth absence in a row due to a groin injury. Head coach DeMeco Ryans said afterward that he's "not certain" if Montgomery will be able to play Thursday against the Colts, per DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com. Montgomery's full session was his second straight going back to last week, and assuming he's trending toward a return to action this week, he's poised to take on a large workload considering fellow RB Woody Marks is in the concussion protocol and was a DNP on Monday.

Demercado rushed seven times for 16 yards and brought in one of two targets for minus-1 yard in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. Demercado opened the game as a reserve in his second appearance in a Texans uniform, but Woody Marks' third-quarter exit due to a concussion left the former in the de facto No. 1 role. That still didn't lead to much opportunity for Demercado in a game during which Houston squandered a 17-0 first-half lead. However, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com reports Marks is unlikely to play in Week 11 due to the short turnaround for a home matchup against the Colts, meaning Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale could have expanded roles in that game unless David Montgomery (groin) is able to suit up.

Boutte failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns. Even with Marvin Harrison (hamstring) out and Jaylin Noel (toe) done for the season, Boutte was targeted one just one of C.J. Stroud's 38 pass attempts versus Cleveland. His 47 snaps on offense were fewer than both Nico Collins (57) and Xavier Hutchinson (51) but 14 more than Tank Dell, though Dell out-targeted Boutte four to one. Boutte popped off for 4-125-2 in Week 9 against the Chargers but has otherwise failed to reach 40 receiving yards in any of his eight other appearances this season.

Harrison (hamstring) was estimated as a non-participant on Monday's practice report. After missing Sunday's loss to the Browns, Harrison opened the new week with another missed practice due to his hamstring issue. If he's unable to return in time for Thursday night's game against the Colts on a short week, Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell likely will soak up the vast majority of the snaps at wideout.

Collins secured nine of 16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. Collins comfortably paced the Texans across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and he added his fifth touchdown of the season on a 12-yard catch in the first quarter. Collins also had a 16-yard reception on Houston's last-gasp drive wiped out by an offensive holding penalty, but he still finished with season highs in receptions and targets. Collins retains an unquestioned No. 1 role in the Texans' prolific air attack, affording him an enticing combination of floor and upside heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

Dell brought in three of four targets for 21 yards and rushed once for no gain in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. One week after posting a 105-yard effort against the Chargers in only his second game since 2024, Dell saw a big downturn in yardage Sunday. Nevertheless, the fact he retained a solid complementary role was encouraging, and the speedy wideout seems to be playing unencumbered by any physical or mental limitations following the recovery from his devastating knee injury. Dell will look to boost his yardage back up in a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

Hutchinson brought in four of nine targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday. Hutchinson, who was checked for a concussion during the fourth quarter, finished second across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets for the Texans. He also recorded a touchdown grab for the third straight game on an 11-yard catch early in the second quarter, and his receiving yardage tally was his highest since Week 5. Hutchinson now sports a 28-345-3 receiving line on 54 targets as he continues to function in a steady complementary role heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

Schultz caught one pass for an 11-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns. While Schultz got into the end zone for the first time this campaign, his catches and targets were new single-game lows for 2026. Schultz has yet to produce more than 45 yards in a game when Nico Collins is healthy this season. The veteran tight end is a low-floor, TD-or-bust fantasy bet.

Jones completed 11 of 22 passes for 108 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while adding five carries for nine yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered. Jones failed to eclipse the 200-yard mark for the fourth straight game while throwing multiple picks for the second time in that span. Neither turnover led to any Dolphins points, and Jones also threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to new interim No. 1 receiver Laquon Treadwell in the second quarter. Jones has completed just 59.6 percent of his passes and has a 7:12 TD:INT across 10 games, and with Indianapolis devoid of any realistic postseason aspirations, it may not be long before Anthony Richardson is given an opportunity under center. However, Joel A. Erickson of The Indy Star reports that head coach Shane Steichen has already named Jones the starter for Thursday's Week 11 road matchup against the Texans.

Taylor rushed 16 times for 83 yards and brought in two of four targets for 20 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Indianapolis. Taylor made it through the trade deadline unscathed after rumors swirled around a possible change of scenery, but the talented back still split plenty of work with rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan, who logged 12 carries. Taylor still remained the No. 1 option and was the only one of the two to see any targets, and the rushing yardage total was his best since Week 7, just before serious trade speculation began. Taylor is staying put for the rest of the campaign, but it seems likely that he'll continue ceding a fair share of touches to McGowan moving forward.

McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 61 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. The rookie had shown well in recent weeks while trade speculation swirled around Jonathan Taylor, and even though the latter ultimately stayed put at the deadline, McGowan still compiled a new career high in rush attempts and rushing yards. The Kentucky product also followed up his first career rushing touchdown in Week 9 against the Cowboys with a four-yard scoring run early in the second quarter Sunday, and McGowan was also productive in his returner role. While Taylor should remain the de facto top backfield option for the Colts, McGowan should remain in an elevated role for what remains of Indianapolis' non-contending season.

Treadwell caught three passes on as many targets for 24 yards and a touchdown during Indianapolis' 24-22 win over Miami on Sunday. Week 10 was the Colts' first game without Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, who were traded to the Chiefs and 49ers, respectively, on Tuesday. Treadwell led all Colts wide receivers with three catches and 52 offensive snaps, and he connected with Daniel Jones for a seven-yard touchdown pass late in the second quarter to give Indianapolis a 14-7 halftime lead. It was the first time Treadwell found the end zone this season, and the 2016 first-rounder figures to maintain a larger role in the offense given the departure of the Colts' top targets at the trade deadline. The Colts will hit the road for Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday, and Houston's defense ranks 28th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing wide receivers.

Warren rushed once for three yards and brought in two of three targets for one yard in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. The new-look Colts offense was without Josh Downs and Keenan Allen after trade-deadline moves, but Warren was still surprisingly uninvolved. Daniel Jones completed only 50.0 percent of his passes and threw for just 108 yards, however, so Warren's minimal production is somewhat understandable in that context. Jones has thrown for under 200 yards in four consecutive games and is playing generally uninspired football, so Warren's fantasy outlook remains shaky for the time being but could improve if Anthony Richardson takes over under center at some point.

Mallory (hamstring) did not participate in Monday's walkthrough practice. Mallory suffered a hamstring injury during Week 10 prep, and he was not cleared to play in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Indianapolis is operating on a short week, so Mallory faces an uphill battle to play against the Texans on Thursday.

availability.comment: Beck was 11-for-18 passing for 108 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions and had one rush for one yard during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams. The Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens after Week 8, and then Gardner Minshew tore the UCL in his right elbow in Week 9, setting the stage for the first appearance (a start) of Beck's career. Beck, a rookie third-rounder, generated just two drives of 30-plus yards among his nine possessions overall, and two others ended in interceptions in Rams territory. He also didn't find much success with his top available skill-position talent, TE Trey McBride, who gathered in all five of his targets for 37 yards. They'll look to improve their rapport next Sunday in Kansas City.

A 2026 fifth-round pick, Virgil started his career buried on the depth chart before moving up due to injuries and trades. It's not quite the same as earning a starting job, but he should see routes and targets all the same in the coming weeks. Virgil has been targeted on 11 of 56 routes (19.6 percent) and caught just three passes for 54 yards in five appearances. He should get plenty of playing time this Sunday against the Rams in what will be the first career start for rookie QB Carson Beck.

Higgins has 18 catches for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets, serving as a complementary receiving option alongside Trey McBride when the Cardinals use multi-TE formations. Higgins figures to stick in that role long-term and won't be of much fantasy interest unless McBride misses time.

McBride will look to bounce back next Sunday at Kansas City.

availability.comment: Mahomes completed 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 15 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. Taking advantage of a controlled environment and a fast track at Mercedes-Benz Stadium -- not to mention the presence of the debuting Josh Downs -- Mahomes repeatedly exploited the vulnerabilities of the Falcons defense throughout the afternoon. The legendary signal-caller showed no ill effects from the elbow injury that he'd suffered in Week 9, and he connected with Emmett Johnson (12, six yards), Downs (18 yards), Cyrus Allen (39 yards) and Andrew Armstrong (43 yards) for his quintet of touchdown passes. Mahomes now has multiple scoring strikes and zero interceptions in three straight games, and Sunday's five TD tosses represented a new season high. Mahomes will take 2,385 passing yards and a 19:4 TD:INT into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. Drawing his first career start due to Kenneth Walker (groin) being sidelined, Johnson put on a pretty convincing impression of his star teammate. Not only did Johnson just get himself over the century mark in rushing yards, but he finished as the team leader in receptions and targets while checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards. Johnson struck from 12 and six yards out for his two receiving TDs, underscoring his considerable versatility. If Walker is unable to garner active status for next Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Cardinals, the Chiefs' ground attack will remain in good hands with Johnson.

Downs secured four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled once but recovered and returned three punts for 10 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. Making his Chiefs debut following three days of practice after arriving via trade from the Colts on Tuesday, Downs looked right at home in the Patrick Mahomes-led offense. The young wideout fully capitalized on the upgrade he saw at quarterback, finishing third in receptions, receiving yards and targets right out of the gate and adding his second touchdown of the season on a difficult 18-yard catch just before halftime. Downs' immediate chemistry with Mahomes is highly welcome news for fantasy managers, and he'll aim to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

Rice brought in five of six targets for 82 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. Rice led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in receptions and targets on a prolific afternoon for the Chiefs' air attack. Rice didn't get in on the scoring fun of a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes, but he still eclipsed 80 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 3. Rice's level of involvement was encouraging given the debuting Josh Downs drew five targets, keeping the former's prospects bright for a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

Worthy failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

Kelce secured both targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday. Kelce recorded a 23-yard catch on the Chiefs' first play from scrimmage, seemingly a harbinger of a productive day. However, the veteran tight end also suffered an ankle injury on the tackle, and although he was able to return to the game, he had only one more reception the rest of the way. Despite the modest numbers, Kelce managed to keep his season-long streak of games with multiple receptions going, and he's averaging a career-best 14.6  per catch heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for two yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Brissett looked like a natural fit in coordinator Declan Doyle's offense despite having only practiced a handful of days with the Ravens following his trade from the Cardinals, amassing his highest passing yardage total since Week 11 of last season. As he'd often done with Trey McBride in Arizona, Brissett focused heavily on the tight-end position in his Baltimore debut, connecting with Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas a combined 11 times for 119 yards. Brissett recorded completions to seven different targets overall, but his one interception did lead to a Chargers touchdown. Brissett's prospects in this offense look bright if his first game is any indication, and he'll look to carry over the momentum into a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday.

Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and brought in all five targets for 10 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Henry was surprisingly stymied by a Chargers defense that had surrendered 4.9 yards per carry on the road coming in. The Ravens also threw an atypically high 49 times in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, leaving Henry with season lows in carries and rushing yards. However, the bruising back salvaged his night with his ninth and 10th rushing touchdowns of the season, which came from two and one yard out, respectively. Henry now has failed to eclipse 58 rushing yards in five consecutive games, but with Brissett significantly reviving Baltimore's air attack in his first start, better days should be ahead for the former in short order, beginning with Sunday's Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

Lane brought in three of 11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Lane was far from efficient during his first opportunity to work with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but he parlayed his career-high target total into a career-best yardage tally. The fact the rookie third-round pick garnered so much of Brissett's attention was certainly encouraging, and Lane could emerge as a much more consistent No. 3 option in the offense in coming weeks.

Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Bateman put together a solid performance during his first opportunity to work with Jacoby Brissett, posting his best receiving yardage total since Week 5. The veteran wideout also recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three games, and two of his three catches went for first downs. Bateman seemed to lay a solid foundation with his new signal-caller, and he'll look to continue building on it in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

Flowers brought in six of seven targets for 74 yards and lost a fumble in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. After being held to just three catches for six yards over the previous two games while Joe Fagnano primarily led the Ravens offense, Flowers got a major reprieve in the form of the debuting Jacoby Brissett. The talented wideout took advantage by finishing second in receptions and receiving yards for Baltimore on the night, but Flowers had the ball stripped from him after a 15-yard catch at the Chargers' 46-yard line with 2:11 remaining. The lost fumble turned out to effectively snuff out the Ravens' chances of realistically getting into position for a potential game-tying field goal, ending the game on a sour night. Nevertheless, the fact Brissett threw for 340 yards in his first game in the offense bodes well for Flowers' prospects as a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday approaches.

Andrews brought in all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night. Andrews eased Jacoby Brissett into his team debut by putting on a pretty convincing Trey McBride impression, as the former mustered season-best totals across all three components of his receiving line. Andrews' instant chemistry with Brissett was certainly encouraging after the Ravens' passing attack's moribund state over the prior two contests, and the veteran tight end could continue thriving in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday.

Young completed 17 of 30 passes for 200 yards without a touchdown or interception in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. He added one rushing yard on his only carry. Chuba Hubbard did most of the heavy lifting on offense for the Panthers, piling up 172 scrimmage yards and both the team's touchdowns. It's the first time this season Young failed to throw a TD, but it was also the first time since Week 6 he avoided committing a turnover. The fourth-year QB will take a 16:6 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash against the Ravens.

Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. The 27-year-old RB kept the Panthers' offense afloat nearly single-handedly, as he set a new career high with 172 scrimmage yards while scoring both the team's TDs, on a two-yard run in the first quarter and a one-yard plunge in the fourth. Hubbard's 80 receiving yards were easily a new career high, topping the 3-57-0 line on three targets he recorded in Week 15 of the 2022 season against the Steelers. Over Hubbard's last six games, he surged to 697 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns, and he'll look keep rolling in a Week 11 clash with the Ravens.

Coker failed to catch any of his four targets in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. While it looked like Coker was going to be in line for a breakout 2026 season after his 8-138-2 receiving performance in the Week 1 opener, Coker has been held to 23 catches for 255 yards and one touchdown over his last seven games. At this point, he can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows something in the box score again. This was a pristine on-paper spot versus New Orleans in the dome, and next Sunday's home date against Baltimore won't be any easier.

McMillan caught three of seven targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans. The seven targets led the Panthers on the afternoon, but the second-year wideout wasn't able to do much with them. The 35 yards were McMillan's lowest total since Week 3, and he'll take a 49-660-3 line on 78 targets through nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Ravens.

Waller caught two of four targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. One week after his 8-90-1 receiving outburst, Waller came back to normalcy in the Panthers' three-man committee at tight end. Waller has big upside, but his ceiling games are difficult to predict. He's been held below 40 yards with no touchdowns in five of nine games this season. Waller will be a low-floor TE2 with upside for Week 11 against the Ravens.

Tremble caught four of five targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. The tight end's five targets tie Chuba Hubbard for second on the team behind Tetairoa McMillan's seven. Tremble has yet to reach 50 receiving yards in a game this season, and his four catches matched his season high. More of a blocker and red-zone specialist, Tremble has very little fantasy appeal in a Carolina offense that likes to use three tight ends.

Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. He added 27 yards on four carries. It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. Lawrence will take a sharp 21:5 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Giants.

Tuten carried the ball 26 times for 88 yards and a touchdown and caught three of four targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over Tennessee. It's the second time this season that Tuten has reached triple-digit scrimmage yards in a game, with both those performances coming since the Jaguars' Week 7 bye. The second-year RB capped the rout with a six-yard TD run in the fourth quarter, extending his scoring streak to four games -- a stretch in which Tuten has racked up 260 rushing yards and three touchdowns on the ground while adding a 9-128-3 line on 10 targets through the air. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 11 against the Giants.

Rodriguez rushed for five yards on four carries in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. Rodriguez was out-carried 26 to four by Bhayshul Tuten, who has very much proven himself as the Jaguars' clear RB1 in one of the league's best offenses. Tuten also out-snapped Rodriguez 52 to 10, while LeQuint Allen (12 snaps) saw more playing time. Rodriguez is little more than a deep-league bench stash should something happen to Tuten.

Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

Meyers caught three of six targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. The six targets were second on the Jaguars behind Parker Washington's nine, but Meyers' longest gain of the day went for only 15 yards. The veteran wideout has also failed to find the end zone in six straight games, a stretch in which he's managed just a 19-256-0 line on 32 targets. Meyers will try to end that drought in a Week 11 clash against the Giants.

Washington caught seven of nine targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

Strange caught two of three targets for nine yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. The Jaguars keep blowing out their opponents, and Strange contributed a three-yard touchdown Sunday but was otherwise not heard from much, as Parker Washington dog-walked the Titans' secondary for 7-152-1 receiving on nine targets. Strange's touchdown grab was his first since Week 1. He remans a locked-in TE1 for fantasy, as he is playing virtually every snap in an elite offense.

McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception while adding six rushes for 34 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. McCarthy continued to look like a competent NFL signal-caller in his third start for the Giants, posting a new career high in passing yards and adding a new season high in rushing yardage. His one touchdown pass was a critical one, as he hit Isaiah Likely over the middle for a 66-yard score just before the midway point of the fourth quarter to erase a 17-14 deficit. McCarthy has displayed excellent chemistry with his top targets, and he'll look to keep his hot streak going against a pass-funnel Jaguars defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and brought in three of four targets for 44 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. Skattebo put together an impressive all-around performance that included a season high in receiving yards. He also exceeded the 75-yard mark on the ground for the third time on the campaign, and he went in for his third and fourth rushing touchdowns of the season on one- and 13-yard runs in the first and third quarters, respectively. Skattebo didn't show any ill effects from the hamstring injury that cost him Sunday's win over the Eagles, and he'll now gear up for a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars' elite run defense on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders. Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington. Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

Fields brought in three of four targets for 62 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Nabers secured five of seven targets for 44 yards and lost a fumble in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. The star wideout finished with less than 50 receiving yards for the second time in five days, and Nabers' late third-quarter lost fumble had significant ramifications. The turnover came at the Commanders' 16-yard line with the Giants down by three, costing  New York a golden opportunity to tie the game at minimum. Nabers' aforementioned pair of mediocre performances have come in the wake of a four-game streak of 100-yard efforts in Weeks 4-7, and he'll look to boost his numbers back up against the Jaguars' pass-funnel defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Likely brought in nine of 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown and fumbled once but recovered in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday. Likely set the pace for the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his figure in the middle category also was a career high. The veteran tight end now has five double-digit target tallies on the campaign, and Thursday's production, which included a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the third quarter, pushed his season line to a robust 55-575-7 line across nine games. All three components already are career-high figures, affording Likely massive momentum heading into a Week 11 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Allen completed 11 of 21 passes for 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception while rushing five times for five yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Allen scored one-yard rushing touchdowns in the first and third quarters, bringing his season total up to 11 rushing TDs. He added his 13th touchdown pass of the campaign on a 45-yard strike to DJ Moore later in the third quarter, and Allen's fourth-quarter interception on third-and-long was basically an arm punt. Heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins, the star QB has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all but one outing this season.

Cook rushed 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown and didn't catch his only target in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Buffalo relied primarily on its ground game in the lopsided victory, as Cook's 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter provided the cherry on top after a pair of one-yard Josh Allen rushing scores helped the Bills pull away. Cook extended his touchdown streak to eight games by scoring his ninth rushing TD over that span. He has topped 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game during the productive stretch, bouncing back effectively after being held to 69 scoreless yards by the Texans in the season opener. Cook has a nice opportunity to keep rolling in Week 11, when the 8-1 Bills host the 1-8 Dolphins.

Moore caught four of six targets for 90 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for four yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Moore's 45-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter accounted for half of his team-high total in receiving yards. This was his most productive outing since Moore went for 100 yards and a TD in his Bills debut, and the veteran wide receiver has chipped in 216 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in three games since returning from a shoulder injury. Josh Allen and James Cook continue to lead Buffalo's offense with their legs, but Moore has re-established himself as Allen's top target in the passing game heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins.

Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.

Shakir caught two of three targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. With Buffalo controlling this one most of the afternoon, Josh Allen attempted just 21 passes and completed only 11 on a day wind gusts played a factor. Shakir's 26 receiving yards were his fewest since Week 3. He's scored just one touchdown this season and has yet to hit 100 yards in a game all year, so the ceiling isn't that high for fantasy while the floor is what he produced Sunday. Shakir is more of fantasy WR4 in PPR-based formats.

Kincaid caught two of three targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets. Kincaid contributed catches of four and 54 yards to finish second on the team in receiving yards behind DJ Moore (90). The 2023 first-round pick has seen his usage fluctuate throughout the campaign, as Kincaid has failed to exceed three targets on five occasions but has drawn at least six looks from Josh Allen in each of the other four games. Kincaid is making the most of his opportunities for a second consecutive regular season, averaging 11.9 yards per target in 2026 after leading all qualified TEs with 11.7 YPT in 2025. Next up for Kincaid is a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins.

Knox caught one of his three targets for seven yards in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Knox continues to receive targets as the No. 2 tight end in the Bills offense. The 30-year-old has consistently struggled to bring in catchable balls over the past few contests but remains a valuable part of Buffalo's 13-personnel packages as a blocker and receiving threat. Knox played 41 offensive snaps in Sunday's game and was on the field for 72 percent of the Bills' offensive plays.

availability.comment: McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed twice for four yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble that was returned for a touchdown. Drawing his first career start as a result of Malik Willis having gone on injured reserve with an abdomen injury earlier in the week, McCord acquitted himself well overall in a favorable matchup. The 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles spread the ball around to nine different targets, and he had a statement three-yard touchdown run on the first play of the fourth quarter when he powered through a pair of defenders and broke the plane despite having his facemask pulled. McCord's one turnover was very costly, however, as it was recovered on the Dolphins' six-yard line and returned for a short touchdown. McCord should only get more comfortable by following up Sunday's solid showing with another week of practice, but he'll draw a tough Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

availability.comment: Dulcich failed to haul in either of his two targets while logging 42 of 69 offensive snaps in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. Second-year signal-caller Kyle McCord threw for 209 yards on 32 attempts in his first NFL start, but he couldn't forge much of a connection with Dulcich, who was held without a catch for the second time this season. With Malik Willis (core) out for at least three more contests while on injured reserve, Dulcich will have more time to build a rapport with McCord, but the tight end was far from a reliable fantasy option even when Willis was directing the offense. Despite playing more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in each of the Dolphins' nine games, Dulcich has been limited to 24 receptions for 270 yards and has yet to find the end zone.

availability.comment: Williams completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. He also rushed five times for 16 yards. Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Swift rushed 12 times for 31 yards and didn't catch his lone target in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. Swift was bottled up by an elite Buccaneers run defense that came into Week 9 allowing a league-low 80 rushing yards per game. He nearly had a fumble in the fourth quarter but was ruled down by contact on a play that the Buccaneers unsuccessfully challenged. Swift's momentum came to an abrupt halt with this season-worst performance, as he failed to reach 70 scrimmage yards for the first time all season after racking up seven touchdowns in the preceding four games. After Chicago's Week 10 bye, Swift could be back to sharing the backfield with Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), who hasn't played since Week 4 but recently returned to practice.

Monangai (thumb/toe) said Monday that he's "on track" to return to action Sunday against the Saints, Courtney Cronin of ESPN reports. Monangai was a limited practice participant Nov. 6, which marked his first on-field work since suffering a turf toe injury Oct. 4 versus the Jets. He still missed his fifth consecutive game as a result of that injury and a right thumb issue, but after a Week 10 bye, he's aiming to resume game action. "The time off definitely helped, but I mean it's going to be there," Monangai relayed about the toe concern. "Offseason, I'll heal it. ... It's something I can manage now." He also mentioned that he'll need the support of plates and orthotics inside his cleats the rest of the campaign. The Bears logged an unofficial practice Monday, which Monangai took part in, and Wednesday's injury report will reveal his initial activity level of Week 11 prep.

Raymond caught four passes for 32 yards on seven targets in Sunday night's 27-24 win over the Bucs. Raymond tied Rome Odunze for second on the team in targets behind Luther Burden (nine), but Burden was injured late in the fourth quarter. If he needs to miss any time, Raymond projects to see elevated snaps alongside Odunze and Colston Loveland. The good news for Burden is he'll have two weeks to heal up with the Bears headed into their bye in Week 10.

Burden (concussion) was spotted participating in the Bears' unofficial practice session Monday, AllCHGO.com reports. Burden was diagnosed with a concussion after making a late exit in the Bears' previous game Nov. 8 against the Buccaneers, but he appears to have made some progress through the five-step protocol since Chicago went on bye for Week 10. Though head coach Ben Johnson hasn't confirmed that Burden has cleared the protocol, if the wideout is deemed a full participant Wednesday in the Bears' first official practice of Week 11, it would be a strong sign that he's trending toward playing Sunday against the Saints.

Odunze caught four of seven targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. Odunze bobbled what should have been an easy touchdown catch and failed to get down inbounds by the time he secured the ball, but he made amends two plays later with his first touchdown catch of the season to cap Chicago's opening drive from nine yards out. He had another critical drop later in the game but still finished second on the team behind Luther Burden (concussion) in targets, catches and receiving yards. Burden exited late in the game, and if Chicago's Week 10 bye doesn't provide the team's leading receiver enough time to clear concussion protocol, Odunze could get an uptick in opportunities in Week 11 against the Saints.

Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Shough completed 25 of 35 targets for 187 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added 25 rushing yards on six carries and was charged with a lost fumble. The second-year QB had more turnovers than TDs for only the second time this season, although his fumble may have been been more Audric Estime's fault, and Shough fell short of 200 passing yards for the third time. Rookie Jordyn Tyson was his top downfield option, catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in a breakout performance, but no other Saint saw more than five targets or hauled in more than three passes. Shough will take a 15:7 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Bears.

Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets. With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.

Estime carried the ball seven times for six yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to Carolina. Travis Etienne returned from IR and led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, although he managed just 34 scrimmage yards, while Alvin Kamara handled five touches and scored two short TDs. Perhaps worse for Estime's role and future value, he was ineffective in short-yardage situations, getting stuffed on three attempts to pick up a first down from two yards out or less, and a miscommunication with Tyler Shough on a handoff led to a lost fumble in the second quarter, although the giveaway was charged to the QB. Estime will try to maintain some share of the workload in a Week 11 meeting with the Bears.

Etienne carried the ball eight times for 14 yards and caught three of five targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. Seeing his first action since Week 3 after recovering from a hamstring strain, the former Jaguar led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, ahead of Audric Estime's eight and Alvin Kamara's five. Etienne wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, while Kamara scored two short TDs. Etienne still appears to be the top option for the team at RB, but if Estime keeps taking short-yardage work and Kamara is the preferred red-zone back, it would put a real ceiling on Etienne's upside. He'll look to claim a bigger share of the workload in Week 11 against the Bears.

Olave caught three of four targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. The game wound up being Jordyn Tyson's breakout performance, as the rookie WR hauled in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards, but that didn't leave much volume for Olave or any other Saint. With Tyler Shough struggling, it's unclear whether the passing game can keep more than one pass catcher fantasy-relevant at a time. Olave sports a 59-774-2 line on 87 targets through nine games, and he'll look to bounce back in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

Tyson caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. That bang you just heard was the sound of the window closing on your chances of acquiring Tyson cheaply in your fantasy league. In just his second career NFL game, Tyson dominated looks from Tyler Shough, as no other New Orleans pass catcher handled more than five targets, hauled in more than three passes or topped 30 receiving yards. It may be tough for the team's struggling offense to keep both Tyson and Chris Olave busy at the same time, so the duo may end up trading big games rather than opening things up for each other, but this kind of volume can't be ignored. Tyson will look for his first career touchdown in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

Johnson caught two passes for 28 yards on three targets in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.

Goff completed 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He added three yards on his only carry. A potential barn burner versus Drake Maye never materialized when the New England quarterback left the game early with an ankle injury, but Goff and the Detroit offense still held up their end of the bargain. Two of Goff's TDs went to Amon-Ra St. Brown, including a 56-yard catch-and-run score in the first quarter, while Isaac TeSlaa also hauled in a 12-yard score in the second. Goff will take an 18:4 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash at home against the Buccaneers.

Gibbs carried the ball 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns while catching seven of eight targets for 99 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots. Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game early for New England, setting the stage for the rout, and Gibbs took full advantage as he set new season highs in receiving yards and scrimmage yards. It's the fourth time in 2026 that the star RB has topped 150 rushing yards, and his fourth game with multiple TDs. Gibbs has amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine contests as he gets ready to face a stingy Buccaneers run defense in Week 11.

St. Brown caught four of five targets for 98 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early. St. Brown took full advantage of the volume he saw however, scoring on a 56-yard catch and run in the first quarter and then taking another short pass from Jared Goff and turning it into a 28-yard TD in the third. It was St. Brown's third multi-TD game of the season but his first since Week 2, and he'll take a 65-755-7 line on 91 targets through nine games into a Week 11 clash with the Buccaneers.

TeSlaa caught two of five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle. It was a quiet day for TeSlaa, with the Lions' offense being powered by usual suspects Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, with the latter duo combining for four touchdowns (three receiving, one rushing). TeSlaa was the other Lions player to find the end zone, which took place early in the second quarter on a 12-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff. It was the first touchdown catch of the season for TeSlaa, who found the end zone six times across 17 regular-season games during his rookie campaign in 2025. He has been the Lions' distant WR3 behind St. Brown and Jameson Williams, and that shouldn't change ahead of the team's Week 11 tilt against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

Williams caught four of seven targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs monopolized the Lions' offense on the day, scoring four of the team's five TDs, and there wasn't much production left over for Williams. The fifth-year wideout has topped 50 receiving yards just three times this season, and he'll take a 32-518-5 line on 51 targets through nine games into a Week 11 battle with the Buccaneers.

LaPorta caught one of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munch. The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early, and LaPorta simply didn't get many chances to make an impact. It was the worst performance of the season for the fourth-year tight end, but LaPorta's gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards or getting into the end zone. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

Mayfield's availability for next Sunday's game against the Lions is in question due to an injury he sustained to his foot and ankle area during the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. While Tampa Bay has been on bye for Week 10, Mayfield has been in and out of a walking boot in recent days in an attempt to rehab the injury, per Garafolo. Though the injury isn't viewed as a long-term concern and a stint on injured reserve isn't in consideration, Mayfield could still be at risk of missing his fourth game of the season in Week 11, after he was sidelined from Weeks 4 through 6 due to a dislocated right thumb. Mayfield has struggled since returning from that injury, completing 25 of 46 pass attempts (54.3 percent) for 307 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while the Buccaneers have embraced a run-heavy attack.

Head coach Todd Bowles said Monday that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following their Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports. Though he hasn't shown any signs of wearing down while he's averaged a healthy 4.9 yards per tote through the Buccaneers' first nine games, Irving has already amassed 167 carries -- fourth-most in the NFL -- and would be on pace for a career-high 315 over the course of a 17-game schedule. Given the success they've found on the ground in recent weeks, the Buccaneers could continue to embrace a run-first attack, but expect Irving to cede a bit more work to backups Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker as Tampa Bay aims to keep their top back healthy for the long haul.

Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards and caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears. Most of Gainwell's 76 scrimmage yards came on a 44-yard catch. He has 304 scrimmage yards over the past three games after recording just 122 scrimmage yards across his first six outings for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving rushed for two touchdowns Sunday and remains the top option in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell has started to make the most of his change-of-pace role in the Buccaneers' run-heavy offense. Gainwell will try to pick up where he left off in Week 11 against the Lions after a Week 10 bye.

Godwin caught two of three targets for 16 yards and added a 12-yard rush during Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears. Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.

Egbuka (foot) caught three of five targets for 38 yards and added a one-yard run in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears. Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.

Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears. Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

Otton caught four of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears. The tight end saw a team-high eight targets, drawing a 26.7 percent target share from Baker Mayfield. It still didn't translate into much in the box score, as Otton remains without a touchdown through nine games. He's turned 38 targets into 23 catches for 211 yards this season and is a low-floor fantasy option most weeks.

Prescott completed 30 of 51 passes for 343 yards with five touchdowns and one interception while rushing four times for seven yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. He also ran for a two-point conversion. Playing catch-up from the second quarter on did wonders for Prescott's fantasy production, as the veteran quarterback sent 38 total targets in the direction of the talented trio of George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy alone. Prescott connected with Pickens for three of his scoring strikes, which went for 35, 39 and five yards. Flournoy (11 yards) and Lamb (one yard) accounted for the final two in the fourth quarter, and Prescott added a two-point conversion run after the final scoring toss with an admirable diving attempt on which he made contact with the pylon with the extended ball. Prescott tied a career high with his TD pass total, while his passing yardage was a season high. He should have an opportunity to put together a successful encore next Sunday, as a Week 11 home matchup with the vulnerable Titans secondary awaits.

Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards and brought in his only target for four yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. Williams had a near monopoly on the Cowboys' running back touches, but he worked hard for everything he got against a talented 49ers front seven. The veteran back averaged under 4.0 yards per carry for the seventh time this season, but he did eclipse 60 rushing yards for the third time in the last four games. Williams will take 692 rushing yards and nine rush TDs -- along with a 25-131-1 receiving line -- into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

Lamb secured seven of 13 targets for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. Despite his own impressive numbers, Lamb played second fiddle to George Pickens for a change, as the latter doubled up the former in receptions and did the same with a yard to spare in receiving yards. Nevertheless, Lamb still put together a solid performance that included his eighth touchdown reception of the season, a spectacular leaping one-handed one-yard grab late in the fourth quarter. Lamb now is up to five consecutive double-digit target tallies and has at least 70 receiving yards in four of the last five contests heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the vulnerable Titans defense.

Pickens brought in 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. After watching fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb have several monster performances through the first half of the season, Pickens stepped up and took his turn in his return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Pickens was peppered with targets from Dak Prescott all afternoon, and the star receiver finished with career-high reception and target totals and a season high in receiving yards. Pickens struck from 35, 39 and five yards out on his trio of scoring grabs, which constituted Dak Prescott's first three TD passes on the day. A now clearly healthy Pickens is up to a 50-678-5 line on 80 targets for the season heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

Flournoy tallied six catches for 71 yards and one touchdown on seven targets during Sunday's loss to San Francisco. He also recovered a fumble. Dallas played catch-up for much of the second half in the offensive slugfest, so quarterback Dak Prescott took to the air 51 times. Flournoy got seven of those targets, finishing third on the team behind George Pickens (18) and CeeDee Lamb (13). Flournoy's six receptions and 71 yards were both his second-highest figures so far this season, and the TD was his third in the past five weeks. That last stat in particular gives him relevance in most fantasy leagues, especially in matchups during which Prescott is expected to air it out often. The Cowboys will seek a much-needed win next Sunday at home against Tennessee.

Ward completed 28 of 39 passes for 231 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. The second-year QB kept his team in the game for three quarters, and Ward connected with Tony Pollard for a 32-yard catch-and-run TD on a checkdown in the fourth quarter that brought the Titans to within one score, only for the Jags to pull away late. Ward's production is slowly creeping up, and he's thrown for 535 yards over the last two games with a 4:1 TD:INT, 68.4 percent completion rate and 6.8 YPA, numbers which represent a big step up from the beginning of the season. He'll look to keep making progress in his development in Week 11 against a vulnerable Cowboys defense.

Pollard carried the ball nine times for 33 yards and caught eight of nine targets for 66 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. The veteran RB fell one yard short of reaching 100 scrimmage yards for a third straight game, and Pollard gave the Titans a brief glimmer of hope in the fourth quarter when he took a checkdown from Cam Ward 32 yards to the house, making the score 30-23. Pollard led the Titans in receptions as he produced season-best numbers through the air, and he could retain elevated usage as a pass catcher if top WRs Carnell Tate (shoulder) and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) miss additional time. Pollard lines up for a potential revenge game in Week 11 against the Cowboys.

Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday that he's hopeful that Tate (shoulder) will return to action in Week 11 versus the Cowboys, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports. Even with the benefit of a Week 9 bye, Tate still wound up being sidelined for a second straight game in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars on account of the shoulder injury. Though Saleh is optimistic that the rookie wideout will be ready to go for the Titans' upcoming game in Dallas, Tate will first need to return to practice in some fashion to make that a reality. Tate remained a non-participant in practice throughout Week 10 prep.

Dike caught two passes for 16 yards on three targets in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He added five rushing yards on one attempt. With Carnell Tate (shoulder) out again, Dike played 54 of 57 offensive snaps against Jacksonville, but his three targets were a distant fifth on the team and represented just an 8.1 percent target share. Outside of his 5-71-1 receiving outburst in Week 8 against Cincinnati, Dike has amassed eight catches for 69 scoreless yards. He's not a reliable fantasy option, though a Week 11 date with Dallas' secondary awaits should Tate remain sidelined.

Ayomanor caught five of 10 targets for 79 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. While he wasn't particularly efficient with the volume, Ayomanor led the Titans in targets and receiving yards on the afternoon, , and the receptions and yardage were both career highs, with Carnell Tate (shoulder) sidelined and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) exiting the contest early. If they both remain on the shelf in Week 11 against the Cowboys, Ayomanor figures to handle an increased role once again. The second-year WR sports an 18-290-1 line on 36 targets through nine games on the year.

Robinson is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jaguars due to an ankle injury. The Titans were already without Carnell Tate (shoulder) Sunday, and the team's receiver depth took another hit when Robinson appeared to sustain the injury late in the third quarter. If Robinson is unable to check back into the contest, he'll finish the game with three catches for 10 yards on four targets.

Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. After a career day last time out in Week 8 against the Bengals, Helm's box score looked more familiar against Jacksonville's stout defense. He's been held below 30 yards in eight of nine games this season and has yet to catch a touchdown. Helm is a member of the large bucket of low-floor TE2 options in fantasy.

availability.comment: Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed seven times for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert made a significant contribution himself to cap off Los Angeles' opening drive of the game, taking off when he couldn't find anyone open and recording a 22-yard rushing touchdown for the first points of the night. The game also marked Herbert's first interception-free performance of the season and gives the beleaguered Chargers air attack something to hang its collective hat on heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

Hampton rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. He also fumbled once but recovered. On the momentous occasion of the Chargers' long-awaited first win of the season, Hampton made a significant contribution with a season-high rushing yardage total. The performance also marked the first time Hampton eclipsed the century mark this season, and he added his fourth rushing touchdown of 2026 on a one-yard power run on fourth down on the first play following the two-minute warning in the first half. Hampton now is up to 474 rushing yards and a 12-63-0 receiving line heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a  night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally was also a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

Kolar brought in all three of his targets for 31 yards in a 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday. Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

Smith (ankle) underwent tests Monday that did not reveal any major injuries, but he will continue to be evaluated during the week, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Smith was checked for a concussion in Sunday's loss to the Bills but was cleared and returned to the game before then suffering an ankle injury. He finished the game 13 of 21 passing for 148 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions. It sounds like Smith has a good chance to suit up next Sunday against the Chargers, but if he's not cleared, then rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line to make the start.

Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.

Hall rushed 11 times for 41 yards and caught all four of his targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. Hall narrowly topped Braelon Allen (eight carries for 40 yards) for the team lead in rushing yards and finished second behind Garrett Wilson (seven catches for 106 yards) in both receptions and receiving yards. While Allen continues to be more efficient as a rusher, Hall's superior receiving ability should help the latter maintain the edge in playing time for a 2-8 Jets team that often finds itself playing catch-up. Rookie QB Cade Klubnik, who played most of the second half Sunday, could be more reliant on check downs to Hall than veteran Geno Smith (ankle) was, but it remains to be seen who will get the nod under center in Week 11 against the Chargers.

Mitchell caught three passes for 59 yards on eight targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. With Garrett Wilson back from his one-game absence Sunday, Mitchell was left fighting for secondary looks. His eight targets were second on the team, trailing Wilson's 14, and Omar Cooper's early-game ankle injury helped Mitchell's volume solidify. If Cooper is going to miss time going forward, Mitchell will be a more comfortable fantasy WR3 play with upside headed into next Sunday's game against the Chargers.

Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. Wilson set a new season high in targets and came one yard short of his Week 3 season high Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. His production came on a mix of passes from Geno Smith (ankle) and rookie Cade Klubnik, the latter of whom saw his first NFL action after Smith exited in the second half. Wilson figures to work as the top target for whomever starts under center in a Week 11 road game against the Chargers.

Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Cooper (ankle) will undergo imaging Monday, Eric Allen of the team's official site reports. Cooper played just one snap before exiting Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after injuring his right ankle. Notably, the rookie first-round pick tweaked the same ankle in the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans and was diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, which resulted in a stint on injured reserve. The Jets are hoping that Cooper avoided as significant of an injury this time around, though even if his imaging yields good news, he still could be hard-pressed to suit up next Sunday versus the Chargers.

Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday. Taylor's four catches were tied with Breece Hall and Isaiah Williams for second most on the Jets behind Garrett Wilson, who turned 14 targets into a 7-106-1 line. It was the third time this season that Taylor recorded at least four catches, with his last instance being Week 7 against the Dolphins (five receptions). The second-year tight end has a 22-167-2 line on 29 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

Nix completed 25 of 37 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. He added two rushing yards on five carries. The Broncos had the home team right where they wanted them heading into the fourth quarter -- holding a lead -- and Nix worked his usual magic over the final 15 minutes, leading back-to-back touchdown drives capped by a nine-yard TD run from Jonah Coleman and a 26-yard strike to Pat Bryant for what proved to be the winning score. Nix did throw his first INT since Week 3 in the win, but he heads into a Week 10 bye with Denver riding a five-game win streak that has taken it to the top of the AFC West.

Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards and caught his only target for four yards during Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina. Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.

Coleman carried the ball 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.

Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

Waddle (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports. After being evaluated for a potential concussion, Waddle is done for the day and will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Raiders, following Denver's Week 10 bye. In his absence Sunday, Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims will handle the team's WR duties versus Carolina.

Bryant caught four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina. Bryant was activated from IR on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury, and he came up big late in Sunday's contest, hauling in a 26-yard TD strike from Bo Nix with less than six minutes left in the fourth quarter for what proved to be the game-winning score. The second-year wideout's clutch play came after Jaylen Waddle (concussion) had left the game, and if a Week 10 bye doesn't give him enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.

Franklin brought in three of four targets for 31 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday. Franklin drew a 27-yard pass interference penalty on the Broncos' second offensive play of the game, but the third-year wide receiver didn't log his first catch until early in the fourth quarter. He has operated in a rotational role for most of the season, and even with Jaylen Waddle in the league's concussion protocol, Franklin will likely maintain that workload following the Broncos' Week 10 bye.

Engram caught four of five targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. The four catches matched Engram's season high, and his 33 yards were his most since Week 5. It goes without saying, but Engram is well off the fantasy radar at tight end. He has 17 catches for 169 yards and one touchdown through nine games, averaging a career-low 18.8 yards per contest.

availability.comment: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble. The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 bye will provide an opportunity to evaluate a QB room consisting of Milton, the recently benched Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. Whichever QB gets the starting nod in Week 11 against the Steelers would benefit from the potential return of Smith or Wicks after the bye.
